questions.question: For $\mathbf X\sim\operatorname{Mult}(n,\mathbf p)$ and integers $n_j\ge0$ with $\sum_jn_j=n$, which expression is $\mathbb{P}(\mathbf X=\mathbf n)$?
What does a $\operatorname{Mult}(n,\mathbf p)$ vector $(X_1,\dots,X_k)$ record?
options: How often each of $k$ categories occurs in $n$ independent trials
The category of each of the $n$ trials, in order
The number of trials until every category has occurred
How often each category occurs in $n$ draws without replacement

questions.question: Each of nine trials produces exactly one label A, B or C. Which procedure gives a multinomial vector of label counts?
options: Run independent trials, changing the label probabilities after each trial
Choose one label randomly, then give that same label to all nine trials
Draw nine labelled cards without replacement from a mixed finite deck
Run independent trials, using the same label probabilities on every trial

questions.question: Let $\mathbf X\sim\operatorname{Mult}(n,\mathbf p)$ with $n\ge1$. For distinct categories $i,j$ with $p_i,p_j>0$, why is $\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j)=-np_ip_j$ negative?
options: Because any two count variables in any probability model have negative covariance
Because the counts for distinct categories are independent
Because a trial assigned to one category cannot also contribute to the other
Because probabilities below one always produce negative covariance

questions.question: Let $(X_1,X_2,X_3)\sim\operatorname{Mult}(7,(0.2,0.3,0.5))$. Which proposed count vector has positive probability?
A fair die is rolled $4$ times; $X_1$ counts ones, $X_2$ counts twos and $X_3$ counts the other faces. What is $\mathbb{P}(X_1=1,X_2=1,X_3=2)$?
$20$ customers independently choose plan A, B or C with probabilities $0.5$, $0.3$ and $0.2$. What are the mean and the variance of the number choosing plan B?
For $\mathbf X\sim\operatorname{Mult}\big(12,(\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\tfrac16)\big)$, what is $\operatorname{Cov}(X_1,X_2)$?
Three independent trials each produce category 1, 2 or 3 with probabilities $(0.5,0.3,0.2)$. Let $X_j$ count outcomes in category $j$. What is $\mathbb{P}((X_1,X_2,X_3)=(2,1,0))$?
$(X_1,X_2,X_3)\sim\operatorname{Mult}\big(8,(0.25,0.25,0.5)\big)$. Which law does $X_1+X_2$ have?

A student claims that the counts in $\mathbf X\sim\operatorname{Mult}(n,\mathbf p)$ are independent because each count has a binomial distribution. Assume $n\ge1$ and at least two category probabilities are positive. Is the claim valid?
options: The claim is valid because the underlying trials are independent
The claim is valid because binomial marginal laws imply independence
The claim fails because the counts share the fixed total $n$
The claim fails only when all category probabilities are equal

questions.question: Let $(X_1,X_2)\sim\operatorname{Mult}(n,(p,1-p))$ with $n\ge1$ and $0<p<1$. A student proposes generating independent $U\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)$ and $V\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,1-p)$ to reproduce this vector. Does the construction work?
options: The construction works because both marginal distributions are correct
The construction works because both generated counts lie between zero and $n$
The construction fails because $U+V$ need not equal $n$

questions.question: Let $(X_1,X_2,X_3)\sim\operatorname{Mult}(n,(p_1,p_2,p_3))$, where all three probabilities are positive and sum to one. For an integer $m$ with $0\le m\le n$, which law does $X_2$ have conditional on $X_1=m$?
For $(X_1,X_2,X_3)\sim\operatorname{Mult}\big(n,(\tfrac13,\tfrac13,\tfrac13)\big)$ with $n\ge1$, what is $\operatorname{Corr}(X_1,X_2)$?
For $\mathbf X\sim\operatorname{Mult}\big(10,(0.1,0.4,0.5)\big)$, compute $\operatorname{Var}(X_1+X_2)$ from the variances and the covariance.
Let $(X_1,X_2,X_3)\sim\operatorname{Mult}(7,(\tfrac17,\tfrac27,\tfrac47))$. What is the probability that category 1 is absent or category 2 is absent, including the possibility that both are absent?

Let $\mathbf X\sim\operatorname{Mult}(n,(\tfrac13,\tfrac13,\tfrac13))$. Nonnegative integers $a,b,c$ satisfy $a+b+c=n$ and $a\ge b+2$. Define $R=\mathbb{P}(\mathbf X=(a-1,b+1,c))/\mathbb{P}(\mathbf X=(a,b,c))$. What is $R$?

For $(X_1,X_2,X_3)\sim\operatorname{Mult}(7,(\tfrac12,\tfrac12,0))$, a student retains only count vectors with $X_1>0$, $X_2>0$ and $X_3=0$, arguing that both positive-probability categories must occur. Which normalisation check diagnoses the error?
options: Retained mass is one; both positive-probability categories must occur
Retained mass is $127/128$; only one endpoint vector was omitted
Retained mass is zero; every retained vector contains the factor $0^0$
Retained mass is $63/64$; two possible endpoint vectors were omitted

questions.question: In six independent trials, category 1 has probability $\tfrac12$ and categories 2 and 3 have probability $\tfrac14$ each; $X_j$ is the number of category-$j$ outcomes. Given that $X_1=4$, how likely is $X_2=1$?
Each of $100$ independent trials produces exactly one of three categories, with probabilities $(0.3,0.3,0.4)$. Let $X_j$ count category-$j$ outcomes. What is $\operatorname{Var}(X_1-X_2)$?
